newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia signs accords to open two free-trade zones.
newsitem.headline: Croatia signs accords to open two free-trade zones.

text.p: Croatia on Monday signed agreements to establish two free-trade zones near the Adriatic ports of Sibenik and Bakar, state news agency Hina reported.

Under the agreement, signed by the Economy Minister Nenad Porges, future users of Podi-Sibenik and Kukuljanovo-Bakar zones are obliged to build the infrastructure in the next year as a condition to win working permits.
Director of Podi-Sibenik Vjeceslav Baranovic said two possible investors, from Croatia and Italy, had expressed interest.
"The Italian investor wants to build a factory of pre-fabricated concrete and the one from Croatia is interested in cutting stone," he told the agency.

The agency said users of four free-trade zones in Croatia are expected to invest roughly half a billion kuna over the next five years and employ up to 2,000 workers. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
